summary: Foundations layer of a deep embedding of TTR's set-theoretic substrate (Cooper 2023, Appendix A1): labels as strings, a three-element Flavour type, a mutually inductive value universe Val / Field / LabelledSet / TTRType (types are first-class values via VType), boolean well-formedness (unique labels), lookup X.l, paths(X) and tpaths(X) with a resolver, single-label path subtraction, initial subpaths, and two worked labelled-set examples checked by four reflexivity Examples. Labelled sets are association lists, with the header explicitly conceding the loss of set extensionality in exchange for decidability and computation; dependent function types are excluded from the mutual inductive (strict positivity) and deferred to TTR_records.v. No substantive theorems live here.

sources.citation: Cooper, R. (2023). From Perception to Communication: A Theory of Types for Action and Meaning. Oxford University Press. Appendix A1 (underlying set theory), A11 (record types).
sources.available: full (at formalizing_formal_semantics repo root, not under papers/)

evidence: Header design note (lines 8-13) concedes the core substitution itself: labelled sets as association lists 'lose the extensionality of sets' — a `changed` core definition per rubric section 2, which caps the verdict at partial.
The A1 constructs actually covered (paths, tpaths, resolution, initial subpaths, lookup) track the source's inductive definitions closely, with Cooper's clauses quoted verbatim in comments.
No headline claim of A1 is proved: the only Qed statements are 4 reflexivity Examples on toy labelled sets; path subtraction is implemented only for the single-label case.
The file's own comment at Field says 'We simplify', and the note at lines 95-97 documents the omission of dependent function types (strict positivity).

determination_rationale: Judged from this pilot's own content: the core A1 definition (labelled set = set of fields) had to be changed to association lists with an external well-formedness predicate, losing extensionality (header's own admission), and TTR's dependent function types could not enter the mutual inductive at all — Val -> TTRType violates strict positivity (class i) and had to be re-founded in TTR_records.v. That is exactly rubric section 4 row 3. Provisional evidence: this is a foundations file with no substantive theorems, so the determination rests on documented encoding moves rather than on proved claims; a quotient/finite-set treatment could conceivably lift the list artifact, but no such formalization exists in the repo.

artifact_classes.description: dependent function types (a:T) -> F(a) excluded from the mutual inductive because (Val -> TTRType) violates strict positivity; documented in-file (lines 95-97) and deferred to TTR_records.v

TTR makes types first-class objects (VType : TTRType -> Val); a shallow rendering would collapse type/value levels in Coq's universe hierarchy, so the file dodges class ii by deep-embedding the whole type system as data

no native extensional finite sets: ZF-with-urelements labelled sets become ordered association lists, set-hood (unique labels) maintained as a separate boolean predicate, extensionality lost (ordering artifact acknowledged in header)

notes: Record produced by the batch audit sweep of 2026-09-05; the file predates the atlas zero-axiom discipline but happens to satisfy it (zero Axiom/Parameter declarations; all four Examples close by reflexivity). Foundations-only file: theorem-level evidence for the TTR pilots lives in TTR_theorems_deep.v / TTR_theorems_shallow.v.
